summary: Struct round-trip turned integers into floats, lost >2^53 precision, dropped non-object payload/result
note: integers below 2^53 FIXED 0.1.119, in the inbound direction only (a Struct a client sends is stored as a JSON integer, so REST reads 42). The rest is DOCUMENTED, not fixed (wave 9, 2026-10-12): `Job.payload`, `Job.result`, `EnqueueRequest.payload` and `CompleteRequest.result` are `google.protobuf.Struct`, which holds only a JSON object, so over gRPC a non-object payload or result (array, string, number, boolean, null) arrives with the field absent (`json_to_struct` returns None). Every number a worker receives is a double (a REST payload with n = 42 arrives as `42.0` in Python, Go and PHP and as `42` in JavaScript; whole values below 2^53 are exact and safe to convert back) and an integer of 2^53 or more can arrive rounded (9007199254740993 -> 9007199254740992.0); REST keeps both exactly (reproduced against production 0.1.122 on 2026-10-12). Why it stays open: the fix needs new proto fields (e.g. `bytes payload_json` on `EnqueueRequest` and `Job`, a result twin on `Job` and `CompleteRequest`) read by the four SDKs, a cross-repo contract change. Workaround: use REST, or wrap the value in an object and send big integers as strings. Documented in docs/guides/grpc-server.md (Payloads and results are `google.protobuf.Struct`) and dataflows/grpc-rest.md (Struct numbers); pinned by `docs_contract_tests::grpc_struct_limits_are_true_and_documented`

summary: The slug length rules disagree: `GET /organizations/check-slug` accepts 1-100 characters (after the trim), `POST /auth/signup/complete` and `POST /organizations` accept 3-50 (signup counts the value as sent, before the trim), and `POST /organizations/generate-slug` can return up to 87; a 1-2 or 51-100 character slug is reported valid and available and is then refused at signup with a 400
path: src/api/handlers/organizations.rs (check_slug, validate_signup_slug_length, generate_slug, with_random_suffix); src/api/handlers/email_login.rs (CompleteSignupRequest); src/models/organization.rs:56
note: FIXED 0.1.124 (2026-10-13, commit `e8265b3`). Found in the wave 9 review while documenting `normalize_signup_slug`. `GET /organizations/check-slug` now applies `validate_signup_slug_length` (3-50 characters, counted as the signup validator counts them, on the trimmed and lower-cased slug) before its character rules, so a 1-2 or 51+ character slug is `valid: false` with `Validation failed: Slug must be 3-50 characters` (the signup request's message, in the form of the endpoint's other format errors) instead of green; it used to take 1-100. `generate-slug` now cuts the base at 50 and, when it adds the suffix, at 43, and the suggestion `check-slug` offers for a reserved or taken slug is cut the same way (`with_random_suffix`), so neither can exceed 50. Deliberately NOT changed: what signup (`CompleteSignupRequest`, 3-50 as sent, before the trim) and `POST /organizations` (`CreateOrganizationRequest` 3-50 plus `validate_slug`) accept. The website trims before both calls, so the two agree; a client that pads a 50-character slug with spaces still gets a green check and a 400 at signup, and padding can still let signup take a 1-2 character slug that `check-slug` calls invalid. Tests: `organizations::tests::test_check_slug_length_matches_signup`, `test_generate_slug_fits_the_signup_length`, `r0124::r0124_check_slug_applies_the_signup_length`; pinned by `docs_contract_tests::signup_slug_rules_agree_is_recorded` The padding gap (signup counted the length before the trim, so "   " was stored as an empty slug) is closed in 0.1.124 too: normalize_signup_slug checks 3-50 after the trim.

summary: `POST /organizations/generate-slug` does not consult `RESERVED_SLUGS`: a name such as `Admin` or `API` yields the slug `admin` or `api`, which `check-slug` reports as reserved and which `POST /organizations` and (since 0.1.123) website signup refuse
note: FIXED 0.1.124 (2026-10-13, commit `e8265b3`). Found in the wave 9 review next to FESF-17. `generate_slug` adds the random suffix (`-` and six hex characters, as for a taken slug) when the base is in `RESERVED_SLUGS` or shorter than 3 characters (`base_needs_suffix`), so `Admin` gives `admin-1f2e3d`, never `admin`. A name with no ASCII letter or digit used to give an empty slug; it now gives `org-` and the suffix (the `org-` prefix the handler already puts before a leading digit). Every generated slug passes `check-slug`, website signup and `POST /organizations` (`SLUG_REGEX` included). A name that only contains a reserved word (`Admin Tools` -> `admin-tools`) is offered as it is. Tests: `organizations::tests::test_generate_slug_never_offers_a_reserved_slug`, `test_generate_slug_without_ascii_letters_is_org_and_a_suffix`, `r0124::r0124_generate_slug_never_offers_a_reserved_or_empty_slug`; pinned by `docs_contract_tests::signup_slug_rules_agree_is_recorded`

summary: gRPC `Enqueue` checks the daily cap, inserts, then increments and deletes the row on a refusal: a worker can claim a job the client was told was refused, a failed delete leaves an uncounted job, and an idempotent replay at the cap is `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` instead of `created: false`
note: FIXED 0.1.126. The idempotency key is looked up first (existing job returned with `created: false`), the daily counter is reserved with `try_increment_daily_jobs` before the INSERT, and the reservation is refunded (`refund_daily_jobs`) when the insert fails or the row already existed, as on REST. Test: `r0126_billing_auth_tests::bill03_grpc_replay_at_daily_cap_returns_existing_job`

summary: The organization token bucket is charged before the API key's per-minute window and a key 429 never refunds it, so one runaway key drains the plan bucket and starves every other key
note: FIXED 0.1.126. The key window is checked first on REST and gRPC; the organization bucket is charged only for a request the key allows. Header tie-break unchanged (organization wins). Test: `r0126_billing_auth_tests::bill04_key_limit_does_not_spend_org_token`

summary: A custom `rate_limit_requests_per_second` / `rate_limit_burst` of 0 is accepted but every enforcer clamps it to 1, so a frozen organization still gets one request per second
note: FIXED 0.1.126. Zero is no longer clamped when the limits are read or cached; `check_token_bucket` refuses before the Lua script when either value is 0 (`429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `Retry-After: 60`; gRPC `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`). The `.max(1)` after that check is only a divisor guard. Test: `r0126_billing_auth_tests::bill05_zero_rate_limit_override_rejects`

summary: `invoice.paid` and `invoice.payment_failed` update every organization with the customer id, ignore which subscription the invoice belongs to and ignore `stripe_last_event_at`, so a redelivered old invoice event overwrites a newer subscription status
note: FIXED 0.1.126. Both require `stripe_subscription_id` to equal the invoice's subscription, skip `plan_tier = 'deleted'`, and skip an invoice older than `stripe_last_event_at`; they still do not advance that clock. Test: `r0126_billing_auth_tests::bill06_stale_invoice_event_does_not_overwrite_subscription_status`

summary: Replacing the verified billing email leaves email-login codes of the old address and the email-login system key (`queues: ["*"]`, refresh lifetime 24 days) valid
note: FIXED 0.1.126. A change of a verified address runs in one transaction with `revoke_email_login_identity`: unused login codes of the old address are marked used and the organization's active `is_system` keys are deactivated (auth-cache entries dropped after the commit); the next login creates a new key. `POST /auth/email/verify` accepts an organization only while the code's address is still its verified billing email. Re-confirming the same address changes nothing. Test: `r0126_billing_auth_tests::auth01_billing_email_change_invalidates_old_login`

summary: Logout wrote the session revocation only to Redis and every check read a missing key, an error or no cache as not revoked, so an `allkeys-lru` eviction or a timed-out GET revived a logged-out session through `/auth/refresh`
note: FIXED 0.1.126. Table `revoked_sessions (sid, expires_at)` is the source of truth; logout writes the row first (failure is 503; expired rows pruned on each logout), then the Redis keys (best effort when the token has a sid). `is_token_revoked(cache, pool, jti, sid)`: a Redis hit is final; for a token with a sid a missing key or a Redis error falls back to Postgres, so a Redis outage no longer logs live sessions out; a token without a sid (before 0.1.114) has only the Redis blacklist and fails closed. A Postgres error is 503 (never 401); an open stream keeps running and re-checks. Sessions logged out before this release are in Redis only. Tests: `r0126_billing_auth_tests::auth02_logout_survives_redis_eviction`, `auth02_redis_outage_checks_revocation_in_postgres`

summary: `/auth/validate` returns `valid: true` for refresh tokens, revoked-key and expired-key tokens (and skips revocation when Redis is absent or failing); `/auth/me` returns organization data for an expired key's unexpired access token
note: FIXED 0.1.126. Both call the middleware's `authenticate_jwt_token` (now `pub(crate)`): access token, revocation, key active and unexpired, organization not deleted. `/auth/validate` answers `valid: false` with the reason for every 401 case and 503/500 when the check could not run; `/auth/me` answers 401/503/500 the same way and reports the key's current `queues` (the stale-queues half of R0126-AUTH-03; `/auth/refresh` still copies the token's list, which no route trusts). Test: `r0126_billing_auth_tests::auth04_validate_and_me_reject_tokens_middleware_rejects`

summary: The API-key cache stores the record read before the slow bcrypt verify and re-reads only `is_active`, so a queue-scope or rate-limit update that commits during the verify is served for `API_KEY_CACHE_TTL_SECS` (60 s)
note: FIXED 0.1.126. The re-read before caching selects `is_active, rate_limit, expires_at, queues` and caches that row (`ApiKeyAuthorizationRow`). Cache invalidation still goes through the reverse bcrypt-prefix pointer (unchanged). Test: `r0126_billing_auth_tests::auth05_api_key_cache_sees_queue_update_during_bcrypt`

summary: `POST /workers/{id}/deregister` and gRPC `Deregister` set every `processing` job of the worker back to `pending` and clear its lease although the handler is still running; another worker claims it and the payload runs twice
note: FIXED 0.1.126. `release_jobs_for_deregistered_worker` releases only jobs whose lease is expired or unset and that have retries left (`retry_count < max_retries`): `pending`, `retry_count + 1`, `last_error` "Worker deregistered", a `retry_scheduled` history row. A live lease stays with the worker until it completes or expires (the offline-worker sweep's rule). Tests: `r0126_jobs_realtime_tests::jobs01_deregister_keeps_live_lease_and_requeues_expired`; `bughunt_regression_tests::w8_jobsapi::w8_worker_counters_count_reported_outcomes_only` now expects `processing`

summary: Completing a `parent_job_id` parent sets the child's `dependencies_met` TRUE from the parent alone, overwriting the FALSE stored for a child that also waits on `job_dependencies` rows; the child runs early and the cancel sweep and parent delete skip it
note: FIXED 0.1.126. All three store `check_job_dependencies_met(id)` and only where it differs (`IS DISTINCT FROM`); a still-blocked child becomes FALSE, not NULL (claim treats NULL as ready). Test: `r0126_jobs_realtime_tests::jobs02_parent_completion_does_not_clear_unmet_dependency`

summary: `update_workflow_progress` runs only when a step becomes `completed` or `failed`; worker failures are `deadletter` and dependency cancels are `cancelled`, so the stored workflow stays `running` with `failed_jobs` 0 until a later transition or the idle sweep
note: FIXED 0.1.126. Migration `20261015120100` replaces the function: the guard is `NEW.status IN ('completed','failed','deadletter','cancelled')`; the recount (which already counted `deadletter` and `cancelled`) and the `status IN ('pending','running')` filter are unchanged, so a terminal workflow stays terminal. Existing rows are not recomputed. Test: `r0126_jobs_realtime_tests::jobs03_deadletter_and_cancelled_update_workflow_progress`

summary: Lease-expiry and offline-worker requeues change `retry_count` and `last_error` but write no `job_history` row (only the dead-letter half of the same sweeps does)
note: FIXED 0.1.126. Both requeue statements are CTEs that insert a `retry_scheduled` row (`error`, `retry_count`, `organization_id` in `details`) from the updated rows; the deregister release writes the same row. Test: `r0126_jobs_realtime_tests::jobs04_lease_and_offline_requeues_write_history`

summary: An automatic retry waiting for its backoff is stored `pending` with a future `scheduled_at`, while a job created with a future `scheduled_at` is `scheduled`; `GET /jobs?status=scheduled` and the `scheduled` / `pending` stats disagree about it
note: FIXED 0.1.126. The retry arm of REST fail, the legacy `fail`, gRPC `Fail` and `ProcessJobs` fail store `scheduled`; `FailByWorkerOutcome.new_status` is `scheduled`; claim already waited on `scheduled_at` and the scheduler's activation turns the job `pending` when due. `will_retry` and `retry_delay_secs` are unchanged. Tests: `r0126_jobs_realtime_tests::jobs05_retry_is_scheduled_until_it_is_due`; `bughunt_regression_tests::grpcq::grpc_dead_letter_keeps_retry_count_like_rest`, `w8_jobsapi::w8_worker_counters_count_reported_outcomes_only` and `integration_tests::test_fail_by_worker_reschedules_with_valid_lease` now expect `scheduled`

summary: WebSocket commands parse only as `{"cmd":"Subscribe"|"Unsubscribe"|"Ping"}`; the Go, Python and PHP SDKs (lowercase `cmd`) and the quickstart (`{type, queues}`) are dropped silently, so those clients receive every event of the organization
note: FIXED 0.1.126 (same defect as R0126-LIVE2-01). `ClientCommand` has a hand-written `Deserialize`: `cmd` or `type`, case-insensitive; `queue` plus `queues`; null, missing and `""` are unset. An unrecognized frame or an invalid queue gets an `Error` event and the socket stays open; `Ping` is answered with a `Ping` event; an out-of-scope queue is ignored silently. Tests: `r0126_jobs_realtime_tests::rt01_websocket_accepts_sdk_and_quickstart_subscribe`, `realtime::tests::test_client_command_deserialization`

summary: The socket keeps one filter that ANDs `queue` and `job_id`, a later queue replaces an earlier one, and an `Unsubscribe` that omits a field clears the other one
note: FIXED 0.1.126 (same defect as R0126-LIVE2-02). The socket holds a list of filters, ORed; one filter ANDs its fields; a subscribe adds one filter per named queue (the `job_id` combined with each); an empty list means everything the scope allows; an unsubscribe removes filters whose named fields all match and nothing when it names nothing. The upgrade query is the first filter; global SSE uses the same matching. Tests: `r0126_jobs_realtime_tests::rt02_subscriptions_are_or_and_unsubscribe_is_partial`, `realtime::tests::test_subscription_list_is_or_and_unsubscribe_keeps_other_filters`

summary: Global SSE `GET /events` stays open with only `system.health` after the Redis subscribe fails or the pub/sub channel closes, so clients think they are still subscribed
note: FIXED 0.1.126. A failed subscribe or a closed channel yields an `error` event and ends the stream (the WebSocket's 1011 behavior); with no Redis configured the stream stays health-only. Test: `r0126_jobs_realtime_tests::rt03_sse_ends_when_the_event_channel_closes`

summary: gRPC `RenewLease` and `ProcessJobs` renew stamp `lease_expires_at` with the application clock taken before the statement has a connection, while the guard and every later fence use Postgres `NOW()`; a pool-acquire stall (up to 30 s) or clock offset commits an already-due expiry and answers success
note: FIXED 0.1.126 (verdict: partly, needs a stall). Both set `NOW() + make_interval(secs => N)` and return the stored value with `RETURNING`, as REST heartbeat does. Test: `r0126_jobs_realtime_tests::rt04_renew_lease_expiry_survives_pool_acquire_wait`

summary: A successful manual retry of a delivery of an auto-disabled outgoing webhook overwrites `last_status` `auto_disabled` with `success`, so the dashboard drops the re-enable banner while the webhook stays `enabled = false` and nothing is delivered
note: FIXED 0.1.126. `record_attempt` keeps `last_status` when it is `auto_disabled`; the marker goes away with the `PUT` that re-enables the webhook. Test: `r0126_jobs_realtime_tests::rt05_retry_keeps_auto_disabled_status`

summary: Workflows, schedules and inbound webhooks accept queue names up to 255 characters (and workflow jobs were not validated at all), but claim, worker registration and `POST /jobs` allow 1-100, so a stored job stays `pending` forever
note: FIXED 0.1.126. The three queue_name fields are 1-100 characters. Each workflow job's queue name is checked against the claim rules (before, only the job count was validated); the other per-job rules (key, priority, max_retries, timeout_seconds) still do not run on create, so existing clients are not newly refused. 65-100 characters stays valid. Tests: `r0126_jobs_realtime_tests::live01_queue_names_match_claim_rules`, `workflow::tests::test_workflow_job_queue_name_matches_claim_rules`

summary: Schedules accept queue names with spaces (length check only); the triggered job can be neither claimed nor listed by queue
note: FIXED 0.1.126. Create applies `validate_queue_name_chars` (letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.`, not starting with `.` or `-`). For a schedule stored before the rule, `trigger` answers 400 without enqueuing, and the cron tick writes a `failed` `schedule_runs` row ("queue name is not claimable") and advances `next_run_at` instead of staying due. Test: `r0126_jobs_realtime_tests::live02_trigger_and_cron_skip_unclaimable_queue`

summary: `POST /webhooks/{org_id}/custom` stores a blank (`""` or whitespace) `idempotency_key` as a real value, so every later blank delivery of the organization returns the first job
note: FIXED 0.1.126. The key goes through `normalize_idempotency_key` as on `POST /jobs`; a blank key is stored as NULL, so each delivery creates its own job. Test: `r0126_jobs_realtime_tests::live03_blank_webhook_idempotency_key_is_null`

summary: WebSocket lowercase `subscribe` / `ping` commands are ignored and nothing reports the drop (live repro of R0126-RT-01)
note: FIXED 0.1.126 together with R0126-RT-01 (one change, see there). Test: `r0126_jobs_realtime_tests::rt01_websocket_accepts_sdk_and_quickstart_subscribe`

summary: `Unsubscribe` with `job_id: null` drops an active job filter when the named queue does not match (live repro of R0126-RT-02)
note: FIXED 0.1.126 together with R0126-RT-02 (one change, see there): `unsubscribe_matches` treats an omitted field as a wildcard only for filters that name the other field. Test: `r0126_jobs_realtime_tests::rt02_subscriptions_are_or_and_unsubscribe_is_partial`

summary: SSE `queue.stats` counts a `scheduled` job as `pending`, while REST `pending_jobs` and gRPC `pending` count only `status = 'pending'`
note: FIXED 0.1.126. `add_queue_stream_count` leaves `scheduled` out of the event. Tests: `r0126_grpc_parity_tests::live2_03_sse_queue_stats_does_not_count_scheduled_as_pending`, `realtime::tests::queue_stream_counts_do_not_treat_scheduled_as_pending`

summary: gRPC `RegisterWorker` accepts queue names up to 255 bytes that REST registration and gRPC `Enqueue` (1-100 characters) reject
note: FIXED 0.1.126. The worker validator allows 1-100 characters, counted as characters; the shared `grpc::validation::validate_queue_name` counts characters, not bytes (cap stays 255 for its other callers). Tests: `r0126_grpc_parity_tests::live2_04_grpc_register_worker_rejects_queue_names_over_100`, `grpc_queue_name_validator_counts_characters_not_bytes`; `worker_service::tests::test_validate_queue_name`

summary: gRPC `Complete` without a `result` stores `{}`, REST stores SQL NULL
note: FIXED 0.1.126. `complete_result_text` returns None for an omitted result (bound as NULL, same SQL text as REST) and the JSON text for a present Struct, `{}` included; size limit unchanged. Tests: `r0126_grpc_parity_tests::live2_05_grpc_complete_without_result_stores_null`, `queue_service::tests::complete_without_result_is_sql_null_not_empty_object`

summary: gRPC `Enqueue` stores `max_retries = -5` as the queue default; REST answers 400 for anything outside 0-100
note: FIXED 0.1.126. A negative value is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` ("Max retries must be between 0 and 100"); 0 remains the queue default because proto3 cannot tell it from an omitted field. Test: `r0126_grpc_parity_tests::live2_06_grpc_enqueue_rejects_negative_max_retries`

summary: gRPC reports a wrong `lease_id` on a live lease as "Lease expired"; REST says the token does not match the current lease
note: FIXED 0.1.126. `processing_lease_miss` returns REST's text ("lease_id does not match the job's current lease; this worker no longer holds it") for a live lease with another token; an expired lease still says "Lease expired", and expiry wins when both apply, as on REST. Same `FAILED_PRECONDITION` / `LEASE_EXPIRED` classes. Tests: `r0126_grpc_parity_tests::live2_07_grpc_lease_mismatch_message_matches_rest`, `queue_service::tests::processing_lease_miss_distinguishes_a_live_mismatch_from_expiry`

summary: gRPC `Heartbeat` rewrites an unknown status to `healthy` and writes it over a real `degraded`; REST rejects it
note: FIXED 0.1.126. An unknown status is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` ("Status must be one of: healthy, degraded, draining, offline"); an empty status keeps the stored one. Tests: `r0126_grpc_parity_tests::live2_08_grpc_heartbeat_rejects_unknown_status`, `worker_service::tests::test_requested_heartbeat_status`

summary: gRPC `Dequeue`/`StreamJobs`/`GetQueueStats` accept queue names of 101-255 characters while `Enqueue`, `RegisterWorker` and REST cap at 100
note: FIXED 0.1.127. The shared validator caps at 100 characters (counted in characters). Production held no longer name. Test: `r0126_grpc_parity_tests::grpc_queue_name_validator_counts_characters_not_bytes`

summary: Dependency-flag recompute calls `check_job_dependencies_met` twice per child (in SET and WHERE) on parent completion and in the scheduler sweep
note: FIXED 0.1.127. Computed once per child in a FROM subquery (VOLATILE function, not inlined); status/parent conditions kept on the updated row. Behavior unchanged. Tests: existing dependency suites, `r0126_jobs_realtime_tests::jobs02_parent_completion_does_not_clear_unmet_dependency`

summary: The outbound webhook client follows redirects: a 301/302/303 turns the signed POST into a bodyless GET and a final 2xx is stored as delivered; a 307/308 re-sends the signed body and `X-Spooled-*` headers to any public `Location`
note: FIXED 0.1.128. The client uses `Policy::none()`: the 3xx is the response, stored with its status code and the error `HTTP 3xx`, and the attempt fails and retries like any other non-2xx. Covers organization webhooks, `POST /outgoing-webhooks/{id}/test` and per-job completion callbacks (one shared builder). The SSRF resolver still validates the connected address. Tests: `http_client::tests::outbound_client_does_not_follow_redirects_to_allowed_hosts`, `http_client::tests::outbound_client_does_not_follow_redirects_to_blocked_hosts`

summary: A manual delivery retry runs beside the in-memory automatic retry and both write the same delivery row (a success is sent again and rewritten as failed)
note: FIXED 0.1.128. `outgoing_webhook_deliveries.retry_claim_token` / `retry_claimed_at`: every retry claims the row with an update that matches the attempts it observed (automatic from attempt 2, and manual), sends only if it won, and writes its outcome only while its token is current. The manual loser is `409 CONFLICT` ("A retry of this delivery is already in progress") and neither sends nor writes. A claim older than two minutes can be taken again; a failed row write clears the claim so the automatic chain continues. The auto-disable threshold (20 deliveries) is unchanged, so the reported auto-disable path did not follow. Tests: `r0128_hooks_tests::hook02_manual_retry_does_not_overlap_the_automatic_retry`, `r0128_followup_tests::failed_delivery_write_releases_the_claim_and_retries`

summary: An inbound custom webhook payload containing U+0000 returns 500 `DATABASE_ERROR` (jsonb refuses it) and the sender retries; `POST /jobs` answers 400
note: FIXED 0.1.128. `validate_custom_payload_size` runs `contains_nul` (string values and object keys): 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` (`payload_contains_nul`) before the insert and the quota reservation. Tests: `r0128_hooks_tests::hook03_nul_in_custom_webhook_payload_is_400`, `webhook::tests::custom_webhook_rejects_nul_in_payload`

summary: Inbound custom webhook rejects queue names the rest of the API accepts (`default`, `admin`, `system`, `internal`, `root`, any name with `..`)
note: FIXED 0.1.128. `CustomWebhookRequest.queue_name` uses `validate_queue_name_chars` only, the rule of `POST /jobs` and claim (a leading `.` or `-` is still 400). Tests: `r0128_hooks_tests::hook04_custom_webhook_queue_names_match_post_jobs`, `webhook::tests::custom_webhook_accepts_the_same_queue_names_as_post_jobs`

summary: The published completion-webhook body (no `id`, with `data.completed_at`) is not the body that is signed and sent
note: FIXED 0.1.128 (documentation only). The sample and OpenAPI describe `{id, event, created_at, data: {job_id, queue_name, status, result | error}}`, the bytes that are signed; no `data.completed_at`. A verifier over the raw body always matched. Test: `r0128_hooks_tests::hook05_completion_webhook_docs_match_the_signed_body`

summary: Restoring a soft-deleted organization with a plan-only `PATCH` keeps its verified billing email even when a live organization now holds it, so email login opens the older organization
note: FIXED 0.1.128. A restore (`deleted` to a plan) that sends no billing email checks the stored verified address with `billing_email_taken`; when a live organization holds it, billing email, `billing_email_verified_at` and `pending_billing_email` are cleared in the same update. An address nobody else holds is kept. No unique index was added: concurrent verifies of one address are not serialized here. Test: `r0128_org_tests::org01_restore_drops_a_verified_email_held_by_a_live_org`

summary: `max_queues` is check-then-insert on the pool: parallel first jobs, schedules and workflows into new queue names all pass the cap
path: src/api/handlers/jobs.rs (enforce_new_queue_on); src/grpc/services/queue_service.rs (enqueue); src/api/handlers/schedules.rs (create); src/api/handlers/workflows.rs (create); src/scheduler/mod.rs (cron_new_queue_refusal); src/api/middleware/limits.rs (queue_name_exists, check_new_queue_limit_generic_conn)
note: FIXED 0.1.128 (rated P2: a quota race of the BE-36 class; keeping an over-cap queue working is documented). `POST /jobs`, `POST /jobs/bulk` and gRPC `Enqueue` insert in a transaction that takes `lock_resource(..., "queues")` when the queue is new, re-read `queue_name_exists`, then re-check the cap (429 / `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`); an existing queue takes no lock. Schedule create, workflow create and the cron tick take the same lock. Tests: `r0128_jobs_tests::org02_new_queue_names_respect_max_queues`, `r0128_followup_tests::schedule_create_shares_the_job_queue_lock`, `r0128_followup_tests::workflow_create_shares_the_job_queue_lock`

summary: Setting a plan on a soft-deleted Stripe customer is rewritten to free: delete keeps `stripe_subscription_id` and a plan-only admin `PATCH` reconciles the canceled subscription over it
note: FIXED 0.1.128. A successful cancel during delete sets `stripe_subscription_id` NULL (status `canceled`); the admin patch reconciles only when the request itself sets a subscription id (`subscription_explicitly_set`). Test: `r0128_org_tests::org03_canceled_subscription_does_not_own_the_plan`

summary: `POST /organizations` commits the organization before its first key, and `POST /auth/signup/complete` burns the signup token before either insert
note: FIXED 0.1.128. Organization and first key are inserted in one transaction (bcrypt runs before it); signup consumes its token in that transaction, after the inserts, so a failed insert (a slug taken in between) leaves the token usable. Tests: `r0128_org_tests::org04_org_and_first_key_and_signup_token_commit_together`, `email_login::tests::test_complete_signup_checks_the_slug_before_it_consumes_the_token`

summary: `GET /api-keys` returns only the 100 newest rows (revoked included), so older live keys cannot be listed or revoked from the dashboard (DASH-30 backend half)
note: FIXED 0.1.128. `limit` (1-100, default 100, clamped) and `offset`; `ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC`; `X-Has-More: true|false` from one extra row (`split_page` / `paged`); the body stays a bare array. The dashboard half (paging UI) is in the dashboard repo. Test: `r0128_org_tests::org05_api_key_list_is_paged_newest_first`

summary: A queue-scoped gRPC `Enqueue` replaying an idempotency key of a job in another queue gets that job's id with `created: false`, and its own job is never stored
note: FIXED 0.1.128 (same defect as R0128-FLOW-06). The lookup reads the stored queue; outside the key's scope the answer is `FAILED_PRECONDITION` "Idempotency key is already in use" and no job id; the `ON CONFLICT` arm is guarded by `queue_in_key_scope`, so the race neither updates nor returns that row. The key stays unique per organization. Test: `r0128_jobs_tests::rt01_grpc_idempotency_replay_outside_queue_scope_hides_the_job`

summary: gRPC `Enqueue` stores a whitespace-only idempotency key, so later blank enqueues collapse onto the first job; REST treats it as no key
note: FIXED 0.1.128. The gRPC key goes through `normalize_idempotency_key` (blank = NULL); a non-blank key is stored as sent. Test: `r0128_jobs_tests::rt02_grpc_whitespace_idempotency_key_is_not_stored`

summary: Expiring a workflow's jobs leaves the workflow `pending` forever and it keeps a `max_workflows` slot; workflow create stores a past `expires_at`
note: FIXED 0.1.128. Workflow create rejects an `expires_at` in the past (400 "expires_at must be in the future"). The expiry sweep captures the workflows of the jobs it deletes and, in the same transaction, finishes each `pending` or `running` one with no active job left: `failed` if a step failed or dead-lettered, `cancelled` if a step was cancelled or removed (or no job is left), with `completed_at`. Tests: `r0128_flow_tests::workflow_create_rejects_a_past_expires_at`, `r0128_flow_tests::expiry_of_the_only_job_cancels_the_workflow`, `r0128_followup_tests::expiry_finishes_a_workflow_with_no_active_job`

summary: `dependency_mode: any` is ignored when one alternative fails through `parent_job_id`, expires, or is retried from the DLQ: the child is cancelled or re-gated although another alternative can still complete
path: src/scheduler/mod.rs (update_job_dependencies parent sweep, expiry sweep); src/api/handlers/jobs.rs (retry_dlq child reset)
note: FIXED 0.1.128. The parent-failure and expiry sweeps keep an `any` child while another `job_dependencies` alternative is not failed, dead-lettered or cancelled (the edge sweep's test); DLQ retry sets `dependencies_met` from `check_job_dependencies_met` for `any` children instead of forcing FALSE. The delete trigger is R0128-SCHED-03. Tests: `r0128_flow_tests::any_mode_child_survives_a_failed_parent`, `r0128_flow_tests::dlq_retry_keeps_a_satisfied_any_child_runnable`

summary: `POST /workflows/{id}/retry` reruns steps the user cancelled (no `last_error` filter)
note: FIXED 0.1.128. Reset failed/deadletter steps and cancelled steps whose `last_error` is one of `DEPENDENCY_CANCEL_REASONS`; a user cancel (NULL) and a delete-trigger cancel stay cancelled, as in job and DLQ retry (invariants #34). The lookup returns id and queue; outside the key's scope `POST /jobs` is 409 "Idempotency key is already in use" (no id), `POST /jobs/bulk` refuses the whole request with the same 409 and creates nothing, and the `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE` is guarded by `queue_in_key_scope`, so the other row is not touched even in a race. An in-scope replay is unchanged (200, `created: false`). note: FIXED 0.1.128. A supplied template goes through `check_payload_size_generic` before the UPDATE: 403 (the text create gives) and the stored template and `next_run_at` stay. An update that sends no template does not re-check the stored one (a grandfathered schedule must not start failing on a rename). summary: Cron `next_run_at` is computed from the batch-start clock with no future check at commit, so a slow pass can store a slot that is already due and enqueue the same occurrence twice
note: FIXED 0.1.128 (the stale batch clock is real; the reported cause, two replicas each writing a failed run, did not hold: the cause is a pass that outlasts the slot). After a successful insert the next run is computed from `clock_timestamp()` at commit (`next_run_after_clock`); the "queue is not claimable" path computes it when it writes. The other failure paths still advance from the batch clock and were not moved into the locked transaction. Test: `r0128_sched_tests::cron_success_stores_a_next_run_after_a_slow_insert`

summary: The delete trigger `cancel_blocked_dependents_of_deleted_job` cancels an `any`-mode child when one alternative is deleted (expiry, purge, DELETE) although another can still complete
note: FIXED 0.1.128. The function is replaced: it locks the dependents (found through the `parent_job_id` and `job_dependencies` indexes as a UNION, `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` in id order), then cancels an `any` child only when no other dependency is outside failed/deadletter/cancelled; `all` children are cancelled as before and the edge to a surviving dependency stays, so the orphan sweep cannot release the child. The lock makes two overlapping deletes of the last two alternatives cancel it. Tests: `r0128_sched_tests::deleting_one_any_mode_alternative_leaves_the_child`, `r0128_followup_tests::overlapping_any_mode_deletes_cancel_the_child`

summary: Dependents (`job_dependencies`) cancelled by the expiry delete get no `job.cancelled` event
